title: Meta Muse History: From Llama to the Muse Agent (2026)
summary: Meta Muse history: Llama 4, the Scale AI deal, MSL, Muse Spark to Muse Wonder, and the Muse agent, with a dated 2013-2026 timeline, safety design and FAQs.
body_markdown:
**Meta Muse** is Meta's personal AI agent. It launched in the US on **September 8, 2026** , and it runs every user's errands inside a private cloud computer that Meta calls the **Muse Secure VM** . A second agent, the **Sentinel** , checks everything that tries to leave that machine. The name "Muse" also covers the model family behind it, from **Muse Spark** (April 8, 2026) to **Muse Wonder** (October 12, 2026).


None of that came from nowhere. Muse is the end point of a twelve-year chain: Facebook's research lab in 2013, the open Llama models from 2023, the Llama 4 stumble in April 2025, a **$14.3 billion** bet on Scale AI and its 28-year-old founder, a new lab called **Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL)** , and a January 2026 experiment in which Meta's product chief, Nat Friedman, started to use an open-source agent called OpenClaw.


This guide joins every link of that chain into one dated, sourced story. It draws on Meta's own posts and filings, the Q3 2026 earnings call, and three long interviews with Alexandr Wang, Meta's Chief AI Officer: a Y Combinator talk (July 29, 2026), Cleo Abram's *Huge Conversations* (October 7, 2026) and the David Senra show (October 11, 2026). Where sources disagree, we show both numbers. Where a claim rests on one speaker, we say so.


> **TL;DR:** Meta Muse is Meta's personal AI agent, launched in the US on September 8, 2026 after a 15-month rebuild that began with a $14.3B Scale AI deal in the wake of the Llama 4 stumble. Each user gets a private Secure VM plus a Sentinel checker agent. Meta says more than 10 million people set it up in about six weeks.[Build a workspace agent you can audit →](https://www.taskade.com/create?entry_kind=content&source=blog&entry=%2Fblog%2Fhistory-of-meta-muse)


*Muse puts the agent in a private machine for one person. Taskade puts agents, projects and automations in one shared workspace. We compare the two designsnear the end of this guide .*

## What Is Meta Muse?


**Meta Muse is a consumer AI agent that does tasks on a person's behalf, such as comparing prices, filling forms, booking travel and checking out with a one-time card.** Meta launched it on September 8, 2026 as "The World's First Personal AI Agent Built for Everyone." It is free for most use, and it runs inside a private, per-user cloud machine.


The word "Muse" confuses people, because Meta uses it for four different things. Here is the short map:


Name What it is First shipped


**Muse** (the agent) The personal agent app, on iOS, Android, muse.ai, Mac and WhatsApp 2026-09-08


**Muse Spark** Meta's first closed frontier model family (1.0 to 1.3) 2026-04-08


**Muse Wonder** The larger model family that Meta calls "our first frontier model" 2026-10-12


**Muse Code** A terminal coding agent for developers 2026-08-05


**Muse Image** Meta's own image model 2026-07-07


**Muse Glimmer** A 30B open-weights model that runs on one consumer GPU 2026-08-10


**Muse Spark Open** An open-weights mixture-of-experts model, 816B total and 42B active parameters 2026-10-15


**Muse Charm** A small keychain device shown at Connect Shown 2026-09-23, due December


**Meta AI** The older assistant brand inside Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and the Meta AI app 2023-09-27


The agent is the product most people mean when they search for "Meta Muse." The rest of this guide calls it **the Muse agent** when the difference matters, and **Muse Spark** or **Muse Wonder** when we mean a model.


What makes the Muse agent different from a chatbot is that it keeps working after you close the app. You give it a goal ("lower my internet bill", "find a pickup for the ID I left on the plane"), and it plans, browses, messages, waits and comes back when it needs a decision. That is the same shift that the[history of AI agents](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-agents-history) traces from 1970s research to the agent loop, and the same category that[what AI agents are](https://www.taskade.com/blog/what-are-ai-agents) explains for beginners.

## Who Built Meta Muse? Alexandr Wang, Nat Friedman and MSL


**Meta Muse was built by Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL), led by Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang, with Nat Friedman leading products and applied research under CEO Mark Zuckerberg.** Wang founded the data company Scale AI at 19 and joined Meta in June 2025 as part of a $14.3 billion deal. Friedman, a former GitHub CEO, set the product's taste.

The people around Muse matter because the product is, by Wang's own account, the work of a small team with one point of view. He describes the core group as "fewer than 200 people" across the model and the product, and calls the result "a single work of art." That figure is his, from the Senra interview, and no Meta filing confirms it. Zuckerberg's public framing is that Muse went "from an idea on a whiteboard to a successful product in just about 8 months."

## Before Muse: FAIR, PyTorch and Facebook M (2013 to 2022)


**Meta's AI history starts on December 9, 2013, when Facebook founded FAIR with Yann LeCun as its director.** FAIR gave the world PyTorch, the framework most AI labs still train on. In 2015 Facebook also tried a personal assistant called M, which was cancelled in January 2018. Muse is, in a real sense, M's second attempt.


FAIR's first decade was a research lab's decade. It published openly, co-founded the Partnership on AI in 2016, and released PyTorch to the public in January 2017. In 2018 Jérôme Pesenti took over as head of FAIR and LeCun became chief AI scientist. When Facebook renamed itself Meta in October 2021, FAIR became "Fundamental AI Research." The lab kept its open habit, and that habit shaped Llama.


The forgotten chapter is **Facebook M** . It lived inside Messenger and promised to book restaurants, buy gifts and get theater tickets. Gary Marcus pointed out on September 22, 2026, two weeks after the Muse launch, that M reached only about 10,000 users, that it later emerged that humans worked behind the scenes, and that the project "ended in sorrow in January 2018, canceled less than three years after it was launched." His question for Muse: would better models change the ending?


Assistant Years Who did the work How it ended


**Facebook M** 2015 to 2018 A model plus human trainers who finished many tasks Cancelled January 2018


**Meta AI** 2023 to now Llama models, then Muse Spark Still live inside Meta's apps


**Muse agent** 2026 to now Muse Spark in a per-user VM, with a Sentinel checker Launched September 8, 2026


The M comparison is fair and also incomplete. M had no model that could read a web page, plan ten steps and recover from a dead end. Muse does. But the human question did come back. In September 2026, 404 Media reported that some Muse phone calls in internal testing were placed by human call-center workers. We cover that inthe trust record .


The **Galactica** episode in November 2022 is the other piece of prehistory. Meta's science model went up and came down in about three days after it produced confident nonsense. Two weeks later ChatGPT launched (see the[OpenAI and ChatGPT history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/openai-chatgpt-history) ). Meta's answer was not a chatbot. It was open weights.

## What Happened to Llama? From LLaMA to the Llama 4 Stumble (2023 to 2025)


**Llama was Meta's open-weights model family from February 2023 to April 2025, and Llama 4 was the last major Llama release.** Llama 4 Scout and Maverick shipped on April 5, 2025, but the release drew criticism over benchmark tuning, and the largest model, Behemoth, never shipped. That stumble is what pushed Zuckerberg to call Alexandr Wang.


For two years, Llama made Meta the center of open AI. LLaMA went to researchers in February 2023, and its weights leaked within days. Llama 2 came in July 2023 with a commercial license and Microsoft as a partner. Llama 3 (April 2024) and Llama 3.1 (July 2024, with a 405B model) put open weights close to the closed frontier. By early 2025, Meta said Llama had passed 1 billion downloads.

The trouble started three days after launch. On April 8, 2025, The Verge and others reported that the Maverick that ranked #2 on LMArena was an "experimental" chat-tuned version, not the build Meta released. The public build ranked far lower once tested. LMArena changed its policy. In May 2025 the Wall Street Journal reported that Behemoth was delayed. It never shipped.


Wang's account of what followed is short. In the Senra interview he says Llama 4 was "not on the trajectory" Meta wanted, that Zuckerberg called him for advice, and that the advice turned into a deal. Meta AI kept growing on Llama underneath (it passed 1 billion monthly users across Meta's apps by May 28, 2025), but the frontier race had moved to reasoning models and agents. ## Why Did Meta Buy 49% of Scale AI? The 2025 Refounding


**On June 12, 2025, Meta put $14.3 billion into Scale AI for a 49% non-voting stake, and Scale's founder Alexandr Wang joined Meta.** Scale said the deal valued it at more than $29 billion. Wang calls it a talent deal, not a product deal: Meta bought the person and a few of his team, and Scale kept running on its own.


Meta already knew Scale. It was a customer for years, and it joined Scale's $1 billion Series F as a new investor in May 2024. In the Senra interview, Wang says Alex Schultz introduced him to Zuckerberg years before the deal, that the first meeting took about a year to schedule, and that the two then talked about every six months. After Llama 4, Zuckerberg asked for advice. Wang says he sent "lots and lots of ideas," and that the talks became a deal in five to six weeks. Those details are his.

Why would a social company pay that much for a data-labeling company? Wang's thesis, as he tells it, is about time. Meta's apps hold the hours people *want* to spend: friends, video, messages. If AI removes the hours people *have* to spend on chores, a world of AI favors the company that owns the leisure. That pitch is also the Muse pitch: "Muse can help save you money and save you time."


He also says Meta "looked like damaged goods" on AI in mid-2025, which is why he saw the move as a refounding rather than a job. Leaving Scale after nine years, he says, was a hard emotional process.


### What Scale Taught Wang, and Where It Shows Up in Muse


Wang's YC talk lays out three lessons from Scale. Each one returns in Muse.


Scale-era lesson What it meant at Scale Where it shows up in Muse


**Find the missing ingredient** In 2016, compute and code were "a button online." Data was not, so Scale became the button In 2026 models are a button. Reliability for people who never code is not, so Muse tries to be that button


**Hold a belief nobody agrees with** Investors doubted a data business "even though our numbers were great" Personal agents, while the industry crowded into coding agents


**Right idea, wrong time** The first YC idea, a medical-care agent, failed Medical claims are a named Muse use case


**Pick the longest steep curve** Ride Moore's law, then AI progress Each AI wave is about 10x the last: self-driving, chatbots, coding agents, then agents for everyone


**Skyscrapers vs diamond mining** Scale was an efficiency business with a linear payoff MSL is a power-law lab, but the 100+ behavior eval sheet is skyscraper work inside it


**Nobody is good at what they never did** New hires needed hands-on rounds Many rounds of from-scratch user tests for first-time agent users


In 2026, Wang says the bottleneck is not model progress: "the bottleneck is diffusing that through the rest of the world." That one sentence is the strategy of Muse. Meta did not try to win the coding-agent race. It tried to get agents to the people who will never open a terminal.

## What Is Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL)? The Memo, the Letter and the Layoffs


**Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL) is Meta's AI organization, created by a Zuckerberg memo on June 30, 2025, with Alexandr Wang as Chief AI Officer.** It holds four groups: TBD Lab for frontier models, FAIR for research, Products and Applied Research under Nat Friedman, and MSL Infra. MSL built every Muse model and the Muse agent.


The founding memo, which CNBC published in full, named Wang as Chief AI Officer to "lead MSL" and named Friedman to head "our work on AI products and applied research." It listed 11 new hires from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic. Press reports that month described offers from $1 million to $100 million. Wang later called the big packages "kind of net neutral" against the equity those researchers left behind at OpenAI and Anthropic, which is his opinion.


A month later, on **July 30, 2025** , Zuckerberg published the public letter "Personal Superintelligence." Its idea is that AI should serve each person's own goals rather than automate everyone out of work. Wang says he, Friedman and others helped write it. That is the line Muse is built on.

## Muse Spark: From Codename Avocado to Spark 1.3 (2026)


**Muse Spark is Meta's first closed frontier model family, released on April 8, 2026 under the codename Avocado.** It replaced Llama inside the Meta AI app and meta.ai, with Instant and Thinking modes. Meta then shipped Spark 1.1 (July 9), 1.2 with Muse Code (August 5) and 1.3 (September 2). The Muse agent launched on Spark.


Muse Spark arrived about nine months after MSL's founding memo, which matches Wang's YC timeline. It was late by some outside measures. On March 12, 2026, the New York Times reported that Avocado had slipped and trailed Google, OpenAI and Anthropic in internal tests. When it shipped on April 8, CNBC reported that Meta's stock rose 6.5% that day. The bigger news was the license: for the first time, Meta's best model shipped without open weights.

**The Muse agent began in early 2026, after Nat Friedman used OpenClaw, the open-source personal agent built by Peter Steinberger.** Friedman later wrote that Meta "built muse from scratch" but that it was "definitely heavily inspired as a product by openclaw." ## How Does Meta Muse Work? Secure VM, Sentinel and Approvals


**Meta Muse works by running an agent and the user's data together inside a private cloud machine, the Muse Secure VM, which has its own browser.** A separate Sentinel agent on the same machine must approve anything that leaves it, and Muse asks the person before sensitive actions such as an email or a purchase. Payments go through one-time cards from Link by Stripe.


Meta's launch post describes the design in plain words. The Secure VM "houses both the agent and a person's data." It is isolated from other users' agents. Credentials for connected services sit in secure storage inside it, and Meta says "Muse has no visibility into people's passwords or payment methods." The Sentinel is "kept apart from Muse at the system level," and "Nothing Muse does reaches the internet unless the Sentinel approves it, and it asks the person for permission when needed."

Three open questions will decide how this chapter reads in a year.


**Will people trust an agent from an ad company?** Meta's answer is architecture: a VM, a Sentinel, an opt-out, a promise that VM data stays out of ad systems, and a Confidential VM where Meta holds no key. The shared-chat exposure in October showed that the risk sits in the features around the vault, not only in the vault itself.


**Will the economics close?** Zuckerberg calls Muse "very compute intensive." Meta's 2026 capex guidance is $135 to $145 billion, and Meta says revenue from new AI businesses could arrive in 2027. A free agent that runs a full machine and browser per user is, by Meta's own description, a costly product to give away.


**Will memory catch up with the vision?** Wang's "second mind" needs an agent that remembers a life, and he names memory as the weak spot today. Muse Wonder's Active Memory is Meta's first public answer.


Muse also closes a loop that opened in 2015. Facebook M tried to run errands with humans behind the curtain and was cancelled in 2018. Eleven years later, Meta shipped the same promise on its own models, inside a private machine, with a second agent watching the first. Whether it lasts depends less on the next model than on the next incident.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Meta Muse


What is Meta Muse?


Meta Muse is Meta's personal AI agent. It launched in the US on September 8, 2026, and it does tasks for you, such as shopping, booking travel, lowering bills and filling forms. Each user gets a private cloud computer called the Muse Secure VM, and a separate Sentinel agent must approve anything that leaves it. Muse is also the name of Meta's model family, from Muse Spark to Muse Wonder.


When did Meta Muse come out?


The Muse agent came out on September 8, 2026, in the US, on iOS, Android, the web at muse.ai and WhatsApp. The first Muse model, Muse Spark, shipped earlier, on April 8, 2026. Canada followed on September 18, Japan on October 23 and Singapore on October 27, 2026.


Who created Meta Muse?


Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL) created Meta Muse. MSL is led by Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang, the founder of Scale AI, who joined Meta in June 2025 as part of a 14.3 billion dollar investment in Scale. Nat Friedman leads AI products and applied research, and Mark Zuckerberg is CEO. Friedman says the product was heavily inspired by the open-source agent OpenClaw but built from scratch.


What model does Meta Muse use?


Meta Muse runs on Meta's own Muse Spark models. Meta's launch post says Muse is powered by Muse Spark, and Alexandr Wang says the launch build was a specially trained version of Muse Spark 1.3. Meta's larger Muse Wonder models, released on October 12, 2026, roll out to paying Muse subscribers first.


Is Meta Muse free?


Yes. Meta says Muse is free for most of what people need. On launch day, Alexandr Wang told CNBC and Axios that Muse also has paid monthly plans of 20 dollars and 100 dollars, depending on usage. TechCrunch reported the plan names as Power and Maximum. Meta's own launch post lists no plan names or prices. Facts checked on 2026-11-07.


Is Meta Muse safe?


Meta Muse has more safety layers than most consumer agents: a private Secure VM per user, a Sentinel agent that approves every outbound action, ask-first rules before purchases and emails, an audit trail, and a forget command. Its first two months also brought an Amazon block, a report of human callers in internal tests, and a shared-chat exposure that led Meta to pause sharing on October 20, 2026. Interactions train Meta's models unless you opt out.


Is Meta Muse open source?


No. The Muse agent, Muse Spark and Muse Wonder are closed. Meta did release two open-weights models: Muse Glimmer, a 30B model under Apache 2.0, on August 10, 2026, and Muse Spark Open, with 816B total and 42B active parameters under a custom Muse Model License, on October 15, 2026.


How does Meta Muse make money?


Meta Muse makes money from paid subscriptions today. On the Q3 2026 call, Zuckerberg said the product should be free for most people, that Meta will build commerce tools to earn a fee on transactions that businesses pay, and that over time Meta can take a percent of the value Muse creates. Muse is also central to the business model for Meta's glasses.


What is the difference between Meta AI and Muse?


Meta AI is the assistant inside Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and the Meta AI app, launched in September 2023. Muse is a separate personal agent app, launched in September 2026, that plans and does tasks from a private Secure VM and keeps working after you close it. Both run on Meta's Muse models since April 2026.


Is Muse available outside the US?


Yes, in a few markets. After the US launch on September 8, 2026, Muse opened in Canada on September 18, Japan on October 23 and Singapore on October 27. Zuckerberg said on October 21, 2026 that Meta has not launched it globally yet because Muse is a compute-intensive service to run.


What happened to Meta's Llama models?


Llama 4, released on April 5, 2025, was Meta's last major Llama release. It drew criticism after an experimental version ranked high on LMArena, and the largest model, Behemoth, never shipped. Meta then invested in Scale AI, founded Meta Superintelligence Labs, and replaced Llama with the closed Muse Spark model on April 8, 2026. Open weights returned with Muse Glimmer and Muse Spark Open.


What are Spaces in Meta Muse?


Spaces are custom experiences that Muse builds inside its app from a description, such as a gift tracker, a school dashboard, a wedding planner or a trip planner. Meta introduced them on November 6, 2026. Connected apps keep each space up to date, and spaces are available everywhere Muse is available. Sharing a space is not available yet.
